;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2020 Paris stabbing attack]]
**A knife attack outside the former [[headquarters]] of the [[satirical]] magazine ''[[Charlie Hebdo]]'' in [[Paris]], [[France]], leaves two people wounded. The building is now used by a television production company, and the two wounded victims are workers of the company. The suspected perpetrator and six other people are taken into custody. The interior minister [[Gérald Darmanin]] says that the stabbing is an [[Islamic extremism|Islamic extremist]] terror attack. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-54302337 (BBC News)]
*[[Boko Haram insurgency]]
**Fifteen security personnel are killed when [[Boko Haram]] [[ambush]] a convoy of vehicles in which [[government of Nigeria|government]] officials were driven in [[Borno State]], [[Nigeria]]. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-09/26/c_139399059.htm (Xinhua)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Chuhuiv An-26 crash]]
**A [[Armed Forces of Ukraine|military]] plane carrying cadets from [[Kharkiv]] Air Force University during a training flight crashes in [[Kharkiv Oblast]], [[Ukraine]], killing 26 people and wounding another person. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-54306090 (BBC News)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario]]
*****The [[Government of Ontario]] is implementing a number of new province-wide restrictions and public health measures aimed at curbing a surge in new cases. Under these rules, bars and restaurants, including nightclubs, are ordered to close at 11:00 p.m. local time and all strip clubs will be closed until further notice. The orders take effect at 12:01 a.m. local time tomorrow. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/toronto/covid-19-coronavirus-ontario-september-25-1.5738636 (CBC)]
****[[Prime Minister of Canada|Prime Minister]] [[Justin Trudeau]] announces that the country has signed a deal with [[AstraZeneca]] to buy up to 20 million doses of its [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.brecorder.com/news/40021455/canada-has-signed-deal-for-astrazeneca-vaccine-candidate-pm (''Business Recorder'')]
****The number of cases in [[Canada]] exceeds 150,000. [https://www.sify.com/news/trudeau-announces-vaccine-pact-as-canada-surpasses-150000-covid-cases-news-international-ujzuTfgjjhfjb.html (Sify.com)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****The United States surpasses seven million cases of COVID-19. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/09/25/health/us-coronavirus-friday/index.html (CNN)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[France]] surpasses 500,000 cases of COVID-19. [https://in.mobile.reuters.com/article/amp/idINP6N2FK01U (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]
****[[Portugal]] reports 899 new daily cases, bringing the cumulative total to 72,055 confirmed cases and 1,936 deaths. Ever since the end of national [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns|lockdown]] in May, this has been the sixth time that the country has registered some record increases in new cases, with all six records occurring during the month of September. [https://covid19.min-saude.pt/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/207_DGS_boletim_20200925.pdf (DGS)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports 7,212 cases, their highest since June 23. [https://www.deccanherald.com/international/world-news-politics/russias-new-coronavirus-cases-hit-highest-since-june-23-892863.html (''Deccan Herald'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****The number of new cases in [[Indonesia]] surges by 4,823 in the last 24 hours, taking the nationwide total to 266,845, a new record for the third consecutive day, while at the same time, the number of recovered patients also rises by a record 4,343, exceeding 196,000. [https://news.detik.com/berita/d-5188031/kasus-positif-dan-sembuh-corona-di-ri-25-september-pecah-rekor (detikNews)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]]
****[[Israel]] tightens restrictions one week after a second [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns|lockdown]] came into effect. Effective this afternoon, all businesses not officially considered essential are ordered closed for the next two weeks, with the possibility of being extended, and travel is restricted to 1 kilometer from people's homes. Other planned rules which would affect protesters and synagogue-goers are not yet approved by parliament. [https://amp.france24.com/en/20200925-israel-tightens-lockdown-as-critics-accuse-netanyahu-of-trying-to-curb-protests (France 24)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
***The number of deaths in [[Brazil]] exceeds 140,000. [https://riotimesonline.com/brazil-news/rio-politics/society/covid-19-brazil-counts-140000-deaths-and-4-68-million-cumulative-cases-september-25th/ (''The Rio Times'')]

;International relations
*[[North Korea–South Korea relations]]
**[[North Korea]]n [[List of leaders of North Korea|leader]] [[Kim Jong-un]] issues an apology to [[South Korea]] over the "unfortunate" shooting death of a South Korean official in disputed [[North Korea-South Korea relations|border]] waters on Tuesday. [https://apnews.com/article/south-korea-shootings-archive-north-korea-seoul-a78597c061c756a3c788de9993fe523f (AP)]

;Law and crime
*[[Juneteenth]]
**At a campaign rally, [[United States President]] [[Donald Trump]] is set to make a speech in [[Atlanta]], [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]], advocating to make Juneteenth a [[Federal holidays in the United States|federal holiday]]. [https://www.foxnews.com/politics/trump-juneteenth-national-holiday (Fox News)]
*[[Inter-American Convention Against Terrorism]]
**The [[Dominican Republic]] assumes the [[President (corporate title)|presidency]] of the  Inter-American Committee Against Terrorism (CICTE). [https://dominicantoday.com/dr/local/2020/09/25/a-first-dominican-republic-assumes-presidency-of-oas-body/ (''Dominican Today'')]
*[[2019–20 Hong Kong protests]]
**[[Hong Kong Police Force|Police]] in [[Hong Kong]] ban a rally planned by the [[Civil Human Rights Front]] (CHRF) to protest the arrest of 12 Hong Kong citizens on grounds of [[COVID-19 prevention]] and "violent acts". The organization said they would appeal the decision. [https://hongkongfp.com/2020/09/25/breaking-hong-kong-police-refuse-to-allow-mass-march-citing-covid-19-restrictions-and-threat-of-violent-acts/ (Hong Kong Free Press)]
*Thousands of protesters, predominantly farmers, block roads and [[Indian Railways|railways]] in [[India]] to protest legislation that would remove [[government of India|government]]-guaranteed grain prices which are paid to farmers who sell their produce to the government. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-india-farms-protests/indian-farmers-block-roads-railways-as-protests-mount-over-farm-bills-idUSKCN26G0IC (Reuters)]
*[[Turkey]] orders the arrest of 82 individuals, including members of the [[Peoples' Democratic Party (Turkey)|Peoples' Democratic Party]], over [[2014 Kurdish riots in Turkey|the violent protests]] against the inaction of the [[Turkish Armed Forces]] in the [[Siege of Kobanî]] in 2014. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-security-kurds/turkey-orders-dozens-of-arrests-including-kurdish-opposition-over-kobani-protests-idUSKCN26G0VY (Reuters)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 United States presidential election]]
**[[Google]] and [[YouTube]] announce that after the polls close on November 3 for the Presidential election, they will stop allowing [[Campaign advertising|political ads]] even if there is confusion or civil unrest while votes are counted. [https://www.nbcnews.com/tech/tech-news/google-youtube-won-t-allow-political-ads-while-votes-are-n1241120 (NBC News)] 
*[[Death and funeral of Ruth Bader Ginsburg]]
**[[Associate Justice of the Supreme Court of the United States|Associate Justice]] [[Ruth Bader Ginsburg]] [[Lying in state|lies in state]] in the [[United States Capitol Building]]. She is both the first woman and the first [[Jewish American]] to receive such an honor. [https://www.cnn.com/politics/live-news/ruth-bader-ginsburg-us-capitol/index.html (CNN)]
